evidence.note: Notomi (2022) argues directly against recent Anglophone rejection of the Seventh Letter and concludes that the traditional attribution to Plato should be respected.
Denyer's Oxford Studies review discusses Burnyeat and Frede's case against authenticity, criticizes details but endorses and amplifies their conclusion that the letter is pseudo-Platonic.

Helfer (2023) treats the Platonic Letters as philosophically serious evidence and reviews the provenance/authenticity problem, illustrating that the collection remains an active scholarly field rather than a closed verdict.

rationale: The Seventh Letter is a paradigmatic live authenticity dispute. Major modern scholars argue forcefully that it is pseudo-Platonic, while other recent specialist scholarship defends Platonic authorship and explicitly challenges the skeptical case. B therefore preserves genuine scholarly disagreement and avoids converting either school into a false consensus.
